narrative:
The model determined that you have a 31% chance of representing a bad credit risk. Because this probability exceeded the bank's acceptance threshold, your loan application was denied.

The three factors that most strongly influenced this outcome were the status of your checking account, the installment rate as a percentage of your disposable income, and the requested loan duration. Your checking account status had the largest impact and pushed the prediction toward bad credit risk. Having a negative balance (under 0 DM) is relatively uncommon among approved applicants—only 12.6% of them show this status, while most maintain either no account or a positive balance. This signaled higher risk to the model.

In contrast, both your installment rate and the 12-month loan duration worked in your favor. Your rate of 2% is lower than the 3% average seen among approved loans, and your shorter duration is well below the 19-month average for successful applications. These elements reduced the predicted risk, but unfortunately they were not enough to overcome the negative signal from your checking account.

You should focus on improving the status of your checking account by bringing it into positive territory before reapplying. Once that improves, your other favorable loan terms may be viewed more positively. Consider speaking with a financial advisor to explore ways to strengthen your overall profile in the meantime.
